My son loved it and my husband loved it too, so I went for it. Since it is a Japanese restaurant inside a department store, the environment was very spacious and clean. As soon as I entered, I was greeted by friendly staff, and I placed my order quickly and conveniently using the table kiosk, and the food was immediately set on the table. Also, you can enjoy more authentic, high-quality sushi through the daily event, so be sure to check it out! Look carefully and enjoy the delicious sushi service. Is it really because of the chef's skill? The freshness and taste of the sushi was so good. And unlike typical sushi restaurants, they give you a soy sauce brush, which is really cool! I only tried the omakase spread at the Tokyo restaurant. It tasted like I was at omakase because I was able to spread it on my own. Don't do it yourself haha. The amount of rice and seasoning was so appropriate that I enjoyed it. Especially the kaiseki meal that came with it was so clean and delicious that I filled my stomach with it. The space is spacious and there are rooms, so I highly recommend it for year-end family gatherings, company dinners, friends' gatherings, lovers' dates, etc. Oh, and we. Baby moms say they want to eat sushi, so you noticed a small sushi restaurant~ I think you can enjoy it comfortably here at Sushi Doku Sinchon branch~ Then, be sure to visit Sinchon sushi restaurant Sushi Doku Sinchon Branch, a cost-effective restaurant recommended by Miya~

reviews.text:
A restaurant specializing in pork cutlet
Located a 5-minute walk from Exit 3 of Sinchon Station.
Embro’s Gyeongyang-style pork cutlet is 9,900 won.

A plate of sweet pork cutlet~
I was torn between light Western style pork cutlet and royal pork cutlet,
I chose light Western food because they said the only difference was the quantity!
For reference, it is said that the King Pork Cutlet comes with two pieces of pork cutlet.
If you like a crispy texture, flip the pork cutlet over right away!
As expected from a king pork cutlet, the main flavor is the sauce rather than the meat.
The sauce has a sweet yet thick texture.
It is a taste that anyone can enjoy.
If the quantity is large, pork cutlet may be more cost-effective.
Cabbage salad, pickled radish, kimchi, rice, and soup are provided along with the pork cutlet.
The soup has an impressive rich flavor, and you can whip up a bowl in no time!
Additionally, unlimited refills are possible.
The cabbage is thinly sliced ​​and has a soft and good texture.
It's a great meal to fill your stomach for a price that doesn't exceed 10,000 won.

Store & Tips & Review
The store is not small and there are window seats, so eating alone is okay!
It's relatively quiet on weekday evenings, so you can eat comfortably.
How to order and pay using a table kiosk~
Sometimes card recognition errors may occur.
In that case, payment can also be made at the counter.
It's a pork cutlet specialty restaurant, but strangely enough, they also sell bulbaek~
However, it is a bit disappointing that there is no pork cutlet bulbaek set.
Instead, set menus such as udon are available.
This is the main branch, and there are branches in other areas as well.
They say it’s a restaurant run by a famous YouTuber…
Who do you think it is?

Visited in July 2020.

This is a Gyeongyang-style pork cutlet restaurant located in the university district of Sinchon. These days, the mainstream trend is Japanese-style thick tonkatsu, so it seems that this type of Japanese-style tonkatsu restaurant has become rare. The price starts at 7,000 won for a basic pork cutlet, and although it is not very cheap, it seems to be a competitive price in its own way. I ordered king pork cutlet (9,900 won). Two large pork cutlets were served, and they were delicious, not too thin and just the right thickness. The sauce is also a sweet, Western-style sauce, so it tastes nostalgic. The portion is quite large, but the amount of rice is small, so it feels like you are filling your stomach with just meat.
The disappointing thing is that the taste is average and there is no significant price advantage. Still, I think this is a restaurant you'll want to visit when you want to eat old-fashioned pork cutlet.

#Ewha Womans University #Daehyeon-dong #Yuyake Tokyo

“It’s nice that they even gave me dessert.”

If you stay in the area you are in for a certain period of time, most people start to think that there are no more good restaurants for the taste they have become accustomed to.
It's the same for me, but since I've been in Ewha Womans University's Sinchon area for a long time, it's not easy to find restaurants that stand out anymore.
This is especially true for pork cutlets.

Yuyake Tokyo was a very popular place with good prices, neat visuals, amazing cost-effectiveness that included appetizers and desserts, and the feel of being in front of a women's college that sold tonkatsu rather than pork cutlet. Has the store recently gone out of business because it doesn't look as clean as it used to and the exterior decorations are gone? I revisited the car because it had changed enough to make me curious.

But I feel worse than before.
In an era of increasing standardization and increasing number of tonkatsu experts, this restaurant's tonkatsu is very disappointing and uncompetitive.
Whether it's sirloin or tenderloin, it's all overcooked, so you can't feel the juiciness of the meat, and you can't help but eat the dry pork with the taste of frying oil.

Instead, it seems that they are still appealing to customers with the system of providing appetizers and desserts and two cheese pork cutlets.
The overall darkness and dull operation of the store contrasts strangely with the dirty windows of the store, and for me it is a factor that discourages me from visiting again.

Customers keep coming in for lunch, so it's still a popular restaurant, but I'm worried about whether it will be able to survive in this competitive era.

It was so delicious that I ate 4 dishes! If anyone is looking for Japanese food, I would confidently recommend it. First of all, this restaurant is popular because it serves the rare agedashi tofu (fried tofu in dashi broth). You should avoid it when you think of crispy fried food, but the fried tofu in Cup Ramen Fried Udon is so soft that it makes you feel like you're eating udon. You can't help but drink a glass of sake. Buri... It's delicious in other places, but it's plain. It's delicious. I'll eat it 3 times! No, but up to 2 times? And although the heating karaage (Japanese fried chicken) is not traditional, the sweet sauce inside makes it appetizing. Later, while scooping up the sauce with a spoon, my mouth gets sore that I find myself reaching for a beer. Also, the nankotsu-age (fried chicken cartilage) salad is crazy.... When you see the part-time worker working hard to make the salad, your mouth starts watering. When you see the menu, eat the cartilage and salad, and feel the crunchy texture in your mouth, you will find yourself sipping sake while dancing on your shoulders without even realizing it.

But everyone, the sight and smell of the nabe ordered by the table next to me was crazy... Please try the nabe... Please... If I go back next time, I'll start with the tofu, followed by the fried nabe rice bowl... This place actually sells a la carte items, but it's so delicious that it feels like a course meal... I'm always looking for a store that serves kaisendon like I see in Japan, without being flashy but using relatively high-quality ingredients without being gimmicky, but it's not easy to find.

I arrived in front of the store in a good mood while listening to GFriend's new songs, Crossroads and Dreamcatcher. The store opened at 12 o'clock, not the usual 11 or 11:30, so I had no choice but to wait outside.

Another of my favorite stores, Hokkaido Butadong Sumire right next door, was open, and it seemed like there were still seats, so I thought about stopping by again, but I decided to just wait a bit and have some Kaisendon, so I waited patiently.

Hokkaido Butadong Sumire is so popular that there is quite a bit of waiting.

At 12 o'clock, when the store door opened, I entered the store with another couple. There were four tables for four people, and there were two people, either the male owner and his wife or a female clerk, who greeted us warmly.

I asked if I could sit at a table for 4 even though I was alone, so I was told to sit down, so I sat down and ordered Kaisendon without even looking at the menu.

First, they brought us wet towels, and while we were waiting, a team of 4 customers also came in and everyone ordered Kaisendon.

That's why they all prepared at once, so after about 20 minutes, the much-anticipated kaisendon came out.

Kaisen-don is made with gamtae, which is used to wrap and eat Kaisen-don, clear soup with good shiitake mushroom flavor instead of the commonly seen miso soup, wasabi, gari, a Japanese pickled ginger, and soy sauce.

When I looked at the kaisendon, it contained tuna, salmon roe, sea urchin roe, sea bream, yellowtail, snow crab paste called kani miso, sweet shrimp, etc. The sashimi was cut quite thickly and was good, but I was a little disappointed because the sea urchin roe and especially the salmon roe were of a small size, which I had first experienced at Kiyohan last time when I heard that such small-sized salmon roe were available.

It's not that I don't like them because they're small, but it's because the smaller ones don't have a lot of flavor and the texture is plain.

First, I dipped the sashimi in soy sauce and topped it with wasabi and floated it with rice. However, the rice did not float easily, so when I looked closely, it felt a bit like rice cake, so I was a little disappointed once again.

Still, the sashimi is good because it is all seasonal fish and thick.

However, as expected, the salmon roe is small in size, so the taste and aroma are relatively flat and you can't really chew it, and the sea urchin roe also doesn't have the rich taste of sea urchin roe, which looks good, but is slightly bitter and doesn't have much of a flavor.

However, the clear shiitake mushroom soup that was served had a nice and clear shiitake mushroom scent, but the taste of shiitake mushrooms was subtle, so it was new and good. Please refill this as well.

It wasn't a large portion, so when I finished it relatively quickly, I was served creme brûlée for dessert, and when I tasted it, the custard was soft and the caramel layer on top was lightly broken and tasted good.

Overall, I stopped by to see if it was the same kaisendon as in Japan, where even though it didn't have the fancy or very diverse ingredients I was looking for, the ingredients were decent. The sashimi was sliced thick and was good, but the salmon roe and sea urchin roe, which seemed to have been added to emphasize the variety and luxury of the toppings, were of poor quality, perhaps due to the price, so I was a little disappointed. Instead, I liked the clear shiitake mushroom soup, which had a good shiitake mushroom scent and taste, and the crème brûlée for dessert. Overall, I thought it was okay, but when I compared it to other Kaisendon restaurants I visited later, I thought it was delicious again because the owner chef felt like he put his heart and soul into preparing it, rather than a sloppy Kaisendon with shallow, gimmicky sashimi.

I was in a good mood because I was really into GFRIEND's new song and choreography, which I like, so I stopped by with excitement. It was a visit that felt a little more disappointing than expected, but after listening to GFRIEND's new song, I felt better again, and it was like a Godja friend giving me a bottle and medicine.

Flat soba uses noodles made of 95% buckwheat and 5% rice, and these noodles are gluten-free and additive-free, making them perfect for health-conscious consumers. The flat, wide noodles boast a chewy texture and are served with tsuyu containing radish, green onion, and lemon along with the rich flavor of buckwheat, creating a harmonious combination of richness and freshness. The price of this menu is set at 13,000 won.

Perilla oil soba is sold for 9,900 won, and this menu is characterized by the fragrant scent of perilla oil. The noodles are cooked with perilla oil and sauce at the table, and during this process, the scent of perilla oil seeps into the noodles, giving them a unique taste. Perilla oil is a traditional Korean ingredient, and combining it with Japanese soba is a very creative attempt.

Basil soba is 12,000 won and is a menu item that stands out for its fragrant basil. Basil is used in pesto sauce, which is made with basil, pine nuts, Parmesan cheese, garlic, and olive oil and mixed with noodles. This menu is especially recommended for those who love basil, and the taste is further enhanced by adding the ponzu sauce provided at the table.

These menus are the result of Soba Research Institute's efforts to explore various variations of buckwheat noodles and breathe new life into traditional Japanese soba. Here, visitors can experience the unique taste of soba that combines tradition and modernity, and the delicate taste and aroma of each menu item stimulates visitors' desire to come back again. Soba Lab's menu goes beyond simple noodle dishes and offers enough charm and satisfaction to be a full meal. reviews.text:
A Chinese restaurant that makes you feel good! You can feel that the friendly staff are an important factor in enjoying a meal. Because it is relatively large, it may not be sensitive to social distancing.
Jjajangmyeon’s signature menu items are men’s jjajang and seafood soy sauce. I also ordered a size between seafood fried rice and sweet and sour pork. At first it seemed like a small portion, but as with most Chinese food, I felt full at the end :D
The sweet and sour pork was thick and not hard, and was fried cleanly, while the men's jjajang was a new type of jjajangmyeon topped with spicy pork bulgogi.
In particular, the sweet and sour pork sauce was so transparent that I thought it was Dongchimi, but it felt different!  The meat was well-marinated with the taste of soy sauce-seasoned pork ribs, so it was not at all different from Jjajangmyeon.  The fried rice was a bit plain, but the seasoning was just right, and the soybean paste was also above average.  :D
Satisfied!

Punggukmyeon is a long-standing noodle mill that started in Daegu and is expanding into areas other than food by diversifying its business. It hasn't been long since it started as a franchise, but thanks to this, people across the country are able to know and enjoy Punggukmyeon more.

The representative menu is called Byeolpyeop Noodles, which is similar to Banquet Noodles. However, Punggukmyeon tastes better than other general banquet noodles due to its unique chewy noodles and broth with a clean aftertaste. Of course, it is expensive for banquet noodles.
Asterisk noodles and bibim noodles seem to be the most popular, while other delicacies such as jjamppong kalguksu and seaweed bibimbap are also popular. Dumplings or bulgogi are also recommended as good side dishes.

There's always not enough food here.
